# Legacy Product End-of-Life & Migration Strategy: Retaining Profitability While Managing Technical Debt

## Executive Summary

The legacy product presents a **classic managed decline problem**: High profitability today (one-third of total profit) masks deteriorating unit economics and growing risk exposure. The tension is between **extracting maximum remaining value** while **minimizing defection to competitors** during migration.

**The Core Dilemma**: 
- **Aggressive sunset** (fast EOL, minimal support) = lower costs, higher near-term risk of large customer defection
- **Indefinite support** (maintain legacy indefinitely) = sustainable revenue but accumulating technical debt, security exposure, and engineering resource drain
- **Optimal path**: **Segmented EOL strategy** that preserves 80–90% of legacy revenue by migrating customers on *their terms*, rebuilding only niche features that drive defection risk, and creating migration incentives that flip the cost-benefit calculation

---

## 1. SITUATION ANALYSIS: LEGACY PRODUCT ECONOMICS & RISK PROFILE

### 1.1 Current State: The Profitability Paradox

```
LEGACY PRODUCT FINANCIALS (BASELINE):

Revenue streams:
├─ Annual recurring revenue (ARR): $15M (est.; one-third of company's $45M total)
├─ Gross margin: 70–75% (high; mature product, minimal feature development)
├─ Profitability: $10.5M–11.25M annual profit (1/3 of company's total ~$30–35M profit)
└─ Customer base: ~200–250 large/mid-market customers (annual contracts $50K–$200K each)

Key metrics:
├─ Net revenue retention: 95% (some churn, but stable base; most customers renew)
├─ Customer concentration: Top 20 customers = 40% of revenue ($6M)
│  └─ Risk: Large customers are most likely to defect if forced to migrate
├─ Average customer tenure: 10–15 years (very loyal; switching cost is high because of niche features)
└─ Profitability per customer: $45K–$60K annually (high; justifies dedicated support)

Cost structure (annual):
├─ Engineering maintenance & security updates: $800K–$1.2M/year
│  └─ Rising 15–20%/year (compliance, security patches, OS/library updates)
├─ Customer support: $1.5M–$2M/year (dedicated team familiar with legacy codebase)
│  └─ Harder to hire new engineers (legacy tech stack; approaching retirement risk)
├─ Infrastructure/hosting: $300K–$400K/year
│  └─ Rising ~8%/year (aging hardware; less efficient than modern stacks)
├─ Compliance/security audits: $200K–$300K/year
│  └─ Rising 20–25%/year (regulatory tightening; legacy system harder to audit)
└─ Total cost of ownership: ~$4M–$4.9M/year (grows faster than revenue decline)

Unit economics trend (3-year projection):
├─ Year 1 (today): $15M ARR, $4M costs, $11M profit (73% margin)
├─ Year 2 (with inflation + security needs): $14.8M ARR (slight churn), $4.6M costs, $10.2M profit (69% margin)
├─ Year 3: $14.5M ARR, $5.2M costs, $9.3M profit (64% margin)
└─ Year 5: $13.5M ARR, $6.5M costs, $7M profit (52% margin) — margin compression visible
    └─ If continued: Year 8 = profitability near zero (costs exceed revenue growth trajectory)

Risk exposure (current):
├─ Technical debt: Codebase is 15–20 years old; relies on deprecated libraries/frameworks
├─ Security vulnerabilities: Legacy platform harder to patch; slower to respond to CVEs
├─ Compliance risk: GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2 audits harder on old platforms; increasing fines/liability
├─ Talent drain: Engineers familiar with legacy tech retiring; difficult to backfill
│  └─ One key engineer retires in 18 months; knowledge transfer is incomplete
├─ Vendor risk: Third-party libraries/integrations no longer supported; forced to maintain forks
└─ Business continuity risk: Major security breach on legacy platform = reputational damage

Customer sentiment (inferred from interviews):
├─ 40% of customers: "Will migrate to new product; miss 2–3 legacy features but okay"
│  └─ These customers will migrate within 12–18 months if incentivized
├─ 35% of customers: "Willing to migrate if the 2–3 niche features are rebuilt in new product"
│  └─ These customers are on the fence; migration depends on feature rebuild
├─ 20% of customers: "Legacy product is critical to our workflow; will not migrate for years"
│  └─ These customers have high switching cost; will defect to competitor if forced
├─ 5% of customers: "No plans to migrate; legacy system is too embedded in our business"
│  └─ These customers represent defection risk; need long-term support guarantee
└─ Implicit threat: "If you sunset legacy, we're evaluating alternatives"

Strategic imperative:
├─ Migrate 70–80% of legacy revenue to new product within 18–24 months
├─ Retain 100% of customers (avoid defection to competitors)
├─ Reduce legacy platform cost of ownership by 60–70% (from $4.9M to ~$1.5–2M by Year 3)
├─ Extend legacy EOL support to 5–7 years (to allow gradual migration for most-loyal customers)
└─ Rebuild only the 3–5 niche features that are defection risks; retire others
```

### 1.2 Niche Feature Analysis: Which Features Must Be Rebuilt vs. Retired

```
FEATURE INVENTORY: LEGACY PRODUCT vs. NEW PRODUCT

The new product (launched 3 years ago) covers ~95% of use cases, but has gaps in 
niche features that a subset of customers depend on.

FEATURE MAPPING:

Feature Category        │ Legacy Product │ New Product │ Usage (% of customers) │ Criticality
────────────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────
Core reporting          │ ✓              │ ✓           │ 100%                 │ CRITICAL
Data export (CSV/Excel) │ ✓              │ ✓           │ 98%                  │ CRITICAL
User management         │ ✓              │ ✓           │ 97%                  │ CRITICAL
Audit logs              │ ✓              │ ✓           │ 95%                  │ HIGH
Mobile app              │ Limited        │ Full        │ 70%                  │ HIGH
Custom dashboards       │ ✓ (limited)    │ ✓ (advanced)│ 85%                  │ MEDIUM
API access              │ Limited        │ ✓ Full      │ 45%                  │ MEDIUM
SSO/SAML                │ ✓              │ ✓           │ 40%                  │ MEDIUM
────────────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────
[NICHE FEATURES BELOW]
────────────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────
Custom SQL queries      │ ✓ Advanced     │ ✗ Limited   │ 18%                  │ HIGH*
Batch ETL/import jobs   │ ✓ Mature       │ ✗ Planned   │ 22%                  │ HIGH*
Legacy data formats     │ ✓ Supports 5   │ ✓ Supports 2│ 12%                  │ MEDIUM*
  (proprietary formats) │                │             │                      │
Time-series analysis    │ ✓ Mature       │ ✗ Beta      │ 8%                   │ HIGH*
  (forecasting, trends) │                │             │                      │
Advanced scheduling     │ ✓ Cron-based   │ ✗ In dev    │ 5%                   │ MEDIUM*
  (complex workflows)   │                │             │                      │
Export to legacy tools  │ ✓ 20+ formats  │ ✓ 5 formats │ 9%                   │ MEDIUM*
  (Tableau, old BI)     │                │             │                      │
Multi-tenancy per       │ ✓ Advanced     │ ✓ Basic     │ 3%                   │ MEDIUM*
  account               │                │             │                      │
────────────────────────┴────────────────┴─────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────

KEY INSIGHT: 5 niche features are blocking migration for 30–40% of customer base.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FEATURE-LEVEL DEFECTION RISK ANALYSIS:

Feature: CUSTOM SQL QUERIES (18% of customers; 35% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Legacy product allows advanced SQL queries on underlying data
├─ New product: Limited to pre-built query templates; no custom SQL
├─ Who uses it: Data engineers, analysts, power users who need flexible querying
├─ Customer sentiment: "This is critical to our workflow. We run custom SQL queries 
│  daily. Without it, we'd have to hire more analysts or switch to a tool that 
│  supports custom SQL."
├─ Defection risk: HIGH (these customers are sophisticated; have alternatives)
├─ Decision: MUST REBUILD in new product (phased approach; see Section 3.2)
├─ Estimated effort: 3–4 engineer-months (query engine + safety/performance guardrails)
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 6–8 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not rebuilt, 5–8% of revenue ($750K–$1.2M) at risk

Feature: BATCH ETL/IMPORT JOBS (22% of customers; 28% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Legacy product supports complex, scheduled data import jobs
│  (SFTP pickup, scheduled runs, error handling, retry logic)
├─ New product: Manual imports only; no scheduling or automation
├─ Who uses it: Ops teams, data analysts, integration engineers
├─ Customer sentiment: "We have 50+ automated import jobs running daily. Rebuilding 
│  this in new product would take weeks of engineering."
├─ Defection risk: HIGH (operational burden of migration is significant)
├─ Decision: MUST REBUILD in new product (phased; prioritize top 20 customers)
├─ Estimated effort: 4–5 engineer-months (job scheduler + connectors + error handling)
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 8–10 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not rebuilt, 6–10% of revenue ($900K–$1.5M) at risk

Feature: TIME-SERIES ANALYSIS (8% of customers; 12% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Legacy product has mature forecasting, trend analysis, seasonality 
│  detection (built over 10+ years; integrates with custom reporting)
├─ New product: Time-series beta available; missing some advanced features (confidence 
│  intervals, anomaly detection, forecasting libraries)
├─ Who uses it: Forecasting analysts, supply chain teams, financial planning
├─ Customer sentiment: "The forecasting in legacy product is industry-leading. The new 
│  product's beta is a step backward. We'd need to rebuild our models elsewhere."
├─ Defection risk: MEDIUM-HIGH (specialized use case; customers have alternatives)
├─ Decision: REBUILD + ENHANCE time-series in new product (prioritize this feature)
├─ Estimated effort: 3–4 engineer-months (add confidence intervals, anomaly detection, 
│  integrate with ML libraries)
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 5–6 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not rebuilt, 2–3% of revenue ($300K–$450K) at risk

Feature: ADVANCED SCHEDULING (5% of customers; 8% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Cron-like syntax for complex, recurring workflows (conditional logic, 
│  error handling, notifications)
├─ New product: Simple scheduling available; no conditional logic
├─ Who uses it: Operations teams, data ops, automation engineers
├─ Customer sentiment: "Legacy product's scheduling is powerful. The new product is 
│  too basic for our use case. We'd need to rebuild workflows in a dedicated scheduler 
│  (like Apache Airflow)."
├─ Defection risk: MEDIUM (workaround exists; rebuild in external tool, not critical)
├─ Decision: REBUILD basic conditional logic (not full parity; defer advanced features)
├─ Estimated effort: 1–2 engineer-months (add if/then logic, retry policies)
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 4–5 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not rebuilt, <1% of revenue ($150K–$200K) at risk

Feature: LEGACY DATA FORMATS (12% of customers; 15% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Legacy product imports 5 proprietary/legacy data formats 
│  (old EDI variants, proprietary binary formats from acquired companies)
├─ New product: Supports 2 of the 5; customers must convert data before import
├─ Who uses it: Customers migrating from legacy systems, data from acquired companies
├─ Customer sentiment: "We have 20 years of data in legacy format. Converting all of 
│  it would be expensive. Can the new product read our legacy format?"
├─ Defection risk: MEDIUM (conversion is feasible but costly; some customers will 
│  avoid migration because of this)
├─ Decision: BUILD connector for 2 most-used legacy formats; offer conversion service 
│  for others (outsource to migration partner)
├─ Estimated effort: 1–2 engineer-months (build 2 new connectors); $50K–100K 
│  outsourced conversion services
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 3–4 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not addressed, 3–5% of revenue ($450K–$750K) at risk

Feature: EXPORT TO LEGACY TOOLS (9% of customers; 11% of legacy revenue)
├─ Current state: Legacy product exports to 20+ BI/analytics tools (Tableau, 
│  Microstrategy, old Cognos variants, etc.)
├─ New product: Exports to 5 modern tools (Tableau, Looker, Power BI, modern stacks)
├─ Who uses it: Analytics teams, BI teams, business users
├─ Customer sentiment: "We use Microstrategy 8.x (old version). The new product doesn't 
│  support it. We'd need to upgrade our BI tool AND migrate to new product."
├─ Defection risk: LOW-MEDIUM (workaround: upgrade BI tool; many customers do this 
│  anyway; not a blocker, but adds friction)
├─ Decision: BUILD connectors for 3 most-used legacy tools (Microstrategy, Cognos, 
│  Qlik Sense old); offer direct Tableau/Looker for others
├─ Estimated effort: <1 engineer-month (build 3 connectors; relatively simple)
├─ Timeline: Available in new product by Month 2–3 of migration program
└─ Competitive risk: If not addressed, 1–2% of revenue ($150K–$300K) at risk

SUMMARY: FEATURE REBUILD ROADMAP

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ FEATURES TO REBUILD (in order of criticality + defection risk) │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                │
│ PRIORITY 1 (MUST BUILD; blocking major defection risk):       │
│ ├─ Custom SQL queries (18% of customers; 8–10% revenue risk)   │
│ │  └─ Timeline: Month 6–8 | Effort: 3–4 eng-months            │
│ │                                                              │
│ └─ Batch ETL/import jobs (22% of customers; 6–10% revenue risk)
│    └─ Timeline: Month 8–10 | Effort: 4–5 eng-months           │
│                                                                │
│ PRIORITY 2 (SHOULD BUILD; addressing pain points):            │
│ ├─ Time-series analysis (8% of customers; 2–3% revenue risk)   │
│ │  └─ Timeline: Month 5–6 | Effort: 3–4 eng-months            │
│ │                                                              │
│ ├─ Legacy data format connectors (12% of customers; 3–5% risk) │
│ │  └─ Timeline: Month 3–4 | Effort: 1–2 eng-months + $50–100K │
│ │                                                              │
│ └─ Legacy BI tool exports (9% of customers; 1–2% revenue risk) │
│    └─ Timeline: Month 2–3 | Effort: <1 eng-month              │
│                                                                │
│ PRIORITY 3 (NICE-TO-HAVE; lower defection risk):              │
│ └─ Advanced scheduling (5% of customers; <1% revenue risk)     │
│    └─ Timeline: Month 4–5 | Effort: 1–2 eng-months            │
│                                                                │
│ NOT REBUILDING (retire; customers have workarounds):          │
│ └─ Multi-tenancy per account (3% of customers; very small)     │
│    └─ Customers can use new product's standard multi-tenancy   │
│    └─ Effort: Not worth rebuilding; offer consulting instead   │
│                                                                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

TOTAL ENGINEERING EFFORT TO REBUILD CRITICAL FEATURES:
├─ Priority 1: 7–9 engineer-months
├─ Priority 2: 8–10 engineer-months
├─ Priority 3: 1–2 engineer-months
└─ Total: ~16–21 engineer-months (over 18 months = feasible with 1–2 dedicated engineers 
   + prioritization of new product roadmap)

Cost to rebuild: ~$600K–800K in engineering + ~$50K–100K in outsourced services 
(data conversion) = ~$700K–900K total

Expected revenue protection: $13.5M–$14.2M of legacy revenue (90–95% retention)
without feature rebuilds, expected migration of only ~$8M–10M (60–67% of legacy 
revenue); with rebuilds, expect ~$12.5M–13.5M (83–90% of legacy revenue)

ROI: Spend $700K–900K to protect $4.5M–5.5M in revenue = 5–7x ROI
```

---

## 2. MIGRATION STRATEGY: SUNSET TIMELINE & SUPPORT POLICY

### 2.1 Recommended Sunset Timeline & Migration Phases

```
MIGRATION TIMELINE: 24-MONTH EOL PROGRAM WITH EXTENDED SUNSET SUPPORT

GOAL: Migrate 70–80% of legacy revenue within 18 months; extend EOL support to 
5 years to allow gradual migration for remaining customers.

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      PHASE 1: FOUNDATION & INCENTIVES                    │
│                           MONTH 0–3 (Current)                           │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                          │
│ GOAL: Announce EOL, communicate roadmap, begin feature rebuilds, design  │
│ migration incentives to flip cost-benefit calculation.                   │
│                                                                          │
│ KEY ACTIVITIES:                                                          │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 0 (Week 1–4): Internal Alignment & Roadmap Finalization           │
│ ├─ Product & Engineering: Finalize feature rebuild roadmap (Section 1.2) │
│ ├─ Finance: Model migration incentive costs vs. retention value          │
│ ├─ Sales: Identify top 20 customers; understand migration blockers       │
│ └─ Legal: Draft EOL terms, SLA changes, data export policies             │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 1 (Week 5–8): EOL Announcement & Customer Communication           │
│ ├─ Executive outreach: CEO/VP calls to top 20 customers                  │
│ │  └─ Message: "Announcing EOL in 5 years. Here's what we're building    │
│ │     to make migration easy. We want to partner with you on this."      │
│ ├─ Announcement email to all legacy customers                            │
│ │  └─ Include: EOL date (60 months/5 years), feature rebuild roadmap,   │
│ │     migration incentives, support commitment                          │
│ ├─ Webinar for customers: Deep dive on new product, roadmap, migration   │
│ │  support, Q&A                                                         │
│ └─ Create customer-facing "Migration Center" (website) with docs, tools, │
│    FAQs, migration timeline templates                                   │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 2 (Week 9–12): Segmentation & Incentive Design                   │
│ ├─ Segment customers by:                                                │
│ │  ├─ Revenue size (Top 20, Mid-tier 20–50, Tail)                       │
│ │  ├─ Niche feature dependency (Custom SQL, ETL, Time-series, etc.)     │
│ │  ├─ Current new product usage (already using, pilot, non-users)       │
│ │  └─ Migration readiness (ready now, ready in 6–12 mo, uncertain)      │
│ ├─ Design migration incentive tiers (see Section 2.2)                    │
│ │  ├─ Tier 1 (Top 20): Custom migration packages; extended transition   │
│ │     period; dedicated support                                         │
│ │  ├─ Tier 2 (Mid-tier): Migration credits; accelerated feature access │
│ │  └─ Tier 3 (Tail): Standard migration; discount on Year 1 new product │
│ └─ Finance review: Incentive cost vs. revenue retention                  │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 3 (Week 13–16): Begin Feature Rebuilds & Pilot Migrations        │
│ ├─ Start Priority 2–3 feature builds (legacy data formats, BI exports)   │
│ ├─ Identify 3–5 pilot customers (willing to migrate early; may need      │
│ │  custom features)                                                     │
│ ├─ Begin data migration pilots (test data export, import, validation)    │
│ └─ Hire migration specialist (dedicated person to lead customer          │
│    migrations)                                                          │
│                                                                          │
│ EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY END OF PHASE 1:                                    │
│ ├─ All legacy customers aware of EOL date                               │
│ ├─ Top 20 customers have executive relationships; understand roadmap    │
│ ├─ Migration incentives finalized; communicated to customers             │
│ ├─ Feature rebuilds underway; first features (legacy data formats) ready │
│ ├─ 1–2 pilot customers actively migrating                               │
│ └─ Churn rate: Stable (announcement may trigger slight uptick; expect    │
│    <2% monthly churn from EOL announcement; most customers wait to see   │
│    roadmap delivery)                                                    │
│                                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              PHASE 2: ACCELERATED FEATURE DELIVERY & MIGRATION            │
│                           MONTH 4–12 (Execution)                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                          │
│ GOAL: Deliver critical features; migrate first cohort (35–40% of        │
│ revenue); establish momentum; prove new product readiness.              │
│                                                                          │
│ KEY ACTIVITIES:                                                          │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 4–5: Priority 3 & 2 Features Ready (BI exports, advanced          │
│ scheduling)                                                              │
│ ├─ Release legacy BI tool connectors (Microstrategy, Cognos, Qlik)      │
│ ├─ Release advanced scheduling (conditional logic, error handling)       │
│ ├─ Customer announcements: "Features you requested are now available"    │
│ ├─ Launch migration for 5–10 mid-tier customers                         │
│ │  └─ These customers are not blocked by missing features               │
│ │  └─ Migration time: 2–4 weeks (with vendor support)                   │
│ └─ Expected result: 10–20 customers (3–5% of revenue) migrated          │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 6–7: Priority 1a Features Ready (Custom SQL queries)              │
│ ├─ Release Custom SQL query engine (safe sandbox mode; performance      │
│ │  limits; approval workflow for complex queries)                       │
│ ├─ Customer announcements: "Custom SQL now available in new product"     │
│ ├─ Webinar: Demo custom SQL features; migration path                     │
│ ├─ Launch migration for 10–15 customers who depend on custom SQL        │
│ │  └─ These customers were blocked on this feature; now unblocked       │
│ │  └─ Migration time: 3–6 weeks (includes custom SQL validation)        │
│ └─ Expected result: 20–35 customers (5–8% of revenue) migrated          │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 8–10: Priority 1b Features Ready (Batch ETL/import jobs)         │
│ ├─ Release scheduling engine for data import jobs (SFTP, connectors,    │
│ │  error handling, retry logic)                                         │
│ ├─ Customer announcements: "Automated data imports now available"        │
│ ├─ Webinar: Demo batch import features; migration assistance            │
│ ├─ Launch migration for 15–20 customers who depend on batch ETL        │
│ │  └─ These customers are not blocked; biggest concern is operational   │
│ │  └─ Vendor provides job definition import tool (exports legacy        │
│ │     jobs, imports to new product with 80%+ compatibility)            │
│ │  └─ Migration time: 4–8 weeks (includes job testing, validation)      │
│ └─ Expected result: 30–45 customers (8–12% of revenue) migrated         │
│                                                                          │
│ Month 11–12: Early Adopter Cohort Complete                              │
│ ├─ Celebrate early migrators: Case studies, testimonials                │
│ ├─ Launch migration for remaining 20–30 customers (mid-tier, tail)      │
│ │  └─ These customers were waiting for proof that new product is ready  │
│ │  └─ Early migrations reduce uncertainty; now confident to migrate     │
│ │  └─ Migration time: 2–6 weeks (depending on complexity)               │
│ ├─ Expected result: 50–75 customers (12–20% of revenue) migrated        │
│ │  total by end of Month 12                                            │
│ └─ Overall: 50–75 cumulative migrations; $1.8M–$3M of legacy revenue    │
│    migrated (12–20% of $15M total)                                     │
│                                                                          │
│ PARALLEL ACTIVITIES (ongoing throughout Phase 2):                       │
│ ├─ Priority 2 Feature Build: Time-series analysis (forecast, anomaly     │
│ │  detection) — ready by Month 5–6                                      │
│ ├─ Migration support expansion: Hire 2–3 migration engineers/consultants│
│ ├─ Customer support: Dedicated hotline for migration questions           │
│ ├─ Data security & compliance: Ensure new product passes legacy         │
│ │  customer audits (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR compliance documentation)        │
│ ├─ Training: New product training sessions for legacy customers          │
│ ├─ Incentive tracking: Monitor which incentives are effective; adjust    │
│ └─ Churn monitoring: Track legacy customer churn; flag high-risk         │
│    customers for sales intervention                                     │
│                                                                          │
│ EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY END OF PHASE 2:                                    │
│ ├─ All critical features (custom SQL, batch ETL, time-series) available │
│ ├─ 50–75 customers (12–20% of revenue) migrated                         │
│ ├─ Case studies & testimonials from early migrants (reduce uncertainty)  │
│ ├─ New product proven in production with legacy customer workloads       │
│ ├─ Legacy product churn: <3% monthly (some customers defecting, but      │
│ │  controlled; most waiting for their turn to migrate)                  │
│ ├─ Confidence high that remaining migrations will be smoother (clear     │
│ │  path forward)                                                        │
│ └─ Remaining legacy revenue: ~$10.5M–12M (70% of baseline; 25–30%       │
│    migrated)                                                            │
│                                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  PHASE 3: FULL MIGRATION EXECUTION                       │
│                           MONTH 13–20 (Scale)                           │
